definition: David Carmel (born 1955) is an Israeli computer scientist specializing in Information retrieval (IR).
details: He is a Distinguished Researcher at the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in Haifa, where his research focuses on IR and generative AI. David is also a Senior Research Fellow at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology. He is an ACM Distinguished Member since 2016 and an SIGIR Academy member since 2025.

explainer.lead: David Carmel is an Israeli computer scientist (born 1955). His work spans computer science.

contributions.name: He led the team that achieved the best Precision@10 score at the TREC conference in the “ad-hoc” Web search track in 2001.

David Carmel contributed to the development of the XML Fragments query language, which adopted a classical IR approach for XML search by embedding the XML query and the XML fragments into the same search space.
David Carmel contributed to the IBM Watson project, which competed against human champions on the television quiz show Jeopardy!
